passages.text: Finally, brothers, we ask and encourage you in the Lord Jesus to live in a way that is pleasing to God, just as you have received from us. This is how you already live, so you should do so all the more.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the believers.
He calls them brothers.
He speaks with authority in the Lord Jesus.
He asks them to live in a way that pleases God.
He encourages them to do this.
He reminds them that they have already received instructions from him and his companions.
He says they already live in this way.
He urges them to do so even more.
passages.original: Λοιπὸν οὖν ἀδελφοί ἐρωτῶμεν ὑμᾶς καὶ παρακαλοῦμεν ἐν Κυρίῳ Ἰησοῦ ἵνα καθὼς παρελάβετε παρ’ ἡμῶν τὸ πῶς δεῖ ὑμᾶς περιπατεῖν καὶ ἀρέσκειν Θεῷ καθὼς καὶ περιπατεῖτε ἵνα περισσεύητε μᾶλλον

passages.text: For you know the instructions we gave you by the authority of the Lord Jesus.
passages.sermon: We gave you instructions.\r\nWe gave these instructions by the authority of the Lord Jesus.\r\nYou know these instructions.
passages.original: οἴδατε γὰρ τίνας παραγγελίας ἐδώκαμεν ὑμῖν διὰ τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: For it is God’s will that you should be holy: You must abstain from sexual immorality; each of you must know how to control his own body in holiness and honor, not in lustful passion like the Gentiles who do not know God; and no one should ever violate or exploit his brother in this regard, because the Lord will avenge all such acts, as we have already told you and solemnly warned you.
passages.sermon:
God wants you to be holy.
You must stay away from sexual immorality.
Each of you must control your own body.
You must live in holiness and honor.
Do not live in passionate lust.
The Gentiles do not know God.
They live in passionate lust.
You must not act like them.
Do not wrong or take advantage of your brother in this matter.
The Lord will punish everyone who does these things.
We have already told you this.
We have warned you about it.
passages.original: Τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν θέλημα τοῦ Θεοῦ ὁ ἁγιασμὸς ὑμῶν ἀπέχεσθαι ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ τῆς πορνείας εἰδέναι ἕκαστον ὑμῶν τὸ ἑαυτοῦ σκεῦος κτᾶσθαι ἐν ἁγιασμῷ καὶ τιμῇ μὴ ἐν πάθει ἐπιθυμίας καθάπερ καὶ τὰ ἔθνη τὰ μὴ εἰδότα τὸν Θεόν τὸ μὴ ὑπερβαίνειν καὶ πλεονεκτεῖν ἐν τῷ πράγματι τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ διότι ἔκδικος Κύριος περὶ πάντων τούτων καθὼς καὶ προείπαμεν ὑμῖν καὶ διεμαρτυράμεθα

passages.text: For God has not called us to impurity, but to holiness.
passages.sermon: God calls us.\r\nGod does not call us to impurity.\r\nGod calls us to holiness.
passages.original: οὐ γὰρ ἐκάλεσεν ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεὸς ἐπὶ ἀκαθαρσίᾳ ἀλλ’ ἐν ἁγιασμῷ

passages.text: Anyone, then, who rejects this command does not reject man but God, the very One who gives you His Holy Spirit.
passages.sermon:
God gives you His Holy Spirit.
God commands you to live in holiness.
If anyone rejects this command, he does not reject a human being.
He rejects God.
God is the One who gives you His Holy Spirit.
passages.original: τοιγαροῦν ὁ ἀθετῶν οὐκ ἄνθρωπον ἀθετεῖ ἀλλὰ τὸν Θεὸν τὸν καὶ διδόντα τὸ Πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ τὸ ἅγιον εἰς ὑμᾶς

passages.text: Now about brotherly love, you do not need anyone to write to you, because you yourselves have been taught by God to love one another.
passages.sermon: God teaches you to love one another.\r\nYou do not need anyone to write to you about brotherly love.\r\nYou already know this because God Himself has taught you.
passages.original: Περὶ δὲ τῆς φιλαδελφίας οὐ χρείαν ἔχετε γράφειν ὑμῖν αὐτοὶ γὰρ ὑμεῖς θεοδίδακτοί ἐστε εἰς τὸ ἀγαπᾶν ἀλλήλους

passages.text: And you are indeed showing this love to all the brothers throughout Macedonia. But we urge you, brothers, to excel more and more and to aspire to live quietly, to attend to your own matters, and to work with your own hands, as we instructed you.
passages.sermon:
You show love to all the brothers in all Macedonia.
We see your love in action.
Brothers, we urge you to do even more.
Try to live quietly.
Take care of your own matters.
Work with your own hands.
We gave you these instructions before.
passages.original: καὶ γὰρ ποιεῖτε αὐτὸ εἰς πάντας τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς τοὺς ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ Μακεδονίᾳ Παρακαλοῦμεν δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀδελφοί περισσεύειν μᾶλλον καὶ φιλοτιμεῖσθαι ἡσυχάζειν καὶ πράσσειν τὰ ἴδια καὶ ἐργάζεσθαι ταῖς ἰδίαις χερσὶν ὑμῶν καθὼς ὑμῖν παρηγγείλαμεν

passages.text: Then you will behave properly toward outsiders, without being dependent on anyone.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote to the Christians in Thessalonica.
He told them how to live among people who are not believers.
He said, “Live in a way that is proper toward those outside the church.”
He also said, “Do not depend on anyone.”
passages.original: ἵνα περιπατῆτε εὐσχημόνως πρὸς τοὺς ἔξω καὶ μηδενὸς χρείαν ἔχητε

passages.text: Brothers, we do not want you to be uninformed about those who sleep in death, so that you will not grieve like the rest, who are without hope.
passages.sermon:
Brothers, I speak to you as fellow believers in Jesus Christ.
I do not want you to be uninformed about those who have died.
Some people do not have hope.
They grieve deeply for those who have died.
You have hope in Christ.
I do not want you to grieve like those who have no hope.
passages.original: Οὐ θέλομεν δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν ἀδελφοί περὶ τῶν κοιμωμένων ἵνα μὴ λυπῆσθε καθὼς καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ οἱ μὴ ἔχοντες ἐλπίδα

passages.text: For since we believe that Jesus died and rose again, we also believe that God will bring with Jesus those who have fallen asleep in Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus died.
Jesus rose again.
We believe this.
God will act through Jesus.
God will bring with Jesus those who have died as believers in Him.
passages.original: εἰ γὰρ πιστεύομεν ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἀπέθανεν καὶ ἀνέστη οὕτως καὶ ὁ Θεὸς τοὺς κοιμηθέντας διὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἄξει σὺν αὐτῷ

passages.text: By the word of the Lord, we declare to you that we who are alive and remain until the coming of the Lord will by no means precede those who have fallen asleep.
passages.sermon:
The Lord gave us this message.
We speak by the word of the Lord.
Some of us will still be alive when the Lord comes.
We who are alive and remain will not go before those who have died.
Those who have died will not be left behind.
passages.original: Τοῦτο γὰρ ὑμῖν λέγομεν ἐν λόγῳ Κυρίου ὅτι ἡμεῖς οἱ ζῶντες οἱ περιλειπόμενοι εἰς τὴν παρουσίαν τοῦ Κυρίου οὐ μὴ φθάσωμεν τοὺς κοιμηθέντας

passages.text: For the Lord Himself will descend from heaven with a loud command, with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God, and the dead in Christ will be the first to rise.
passages.sermon:
The Lord Jesus is the Son of God.
The Lord Himself will come down from heaven.
He will give a loud command.
An archangel will speak with a powerful voice.
God’s trumpet will sound.
The dead who belong to Christ will rise first.
passages.original: ὅτι αὐτὸς ὁ Κύριος ἐν κελεύσματι ἐν φωνῇ ἀρχαγγέλου καὶ ἐν σάλπιγγι Θεοῦ καταβήσεται ἀπ’ οὐρανοῦ καὶ οἱ νεκροὶ ἐν Χριστῷ ἀναστήσονται πρῶτον

passages.text: After that, we who are alive and remain will be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air. And so we will always be with the Lord.
passages.sermon:
We who are alive and remain will be caught up together with the dead in Christ.
We will meet the Lord in the air.
We will be in the clouds when we meet Him.
We will always be with the Lord after that.
passages.original: ἔπειτα ἡμεῖς οἱ ζῶντες οἱ περιλειπόμενοι ἅμα σὺν αὐτοῖς ἁρπαγησόμεθα ἐν νεφέλαις εἰς ἀπάντησιν τοῦ Κυρίου εἰς ἀέρα καὶ οὕτως πάντοτε σὺν Κυρίῳ ἐσόμεθα

passages.text: Therefore encourage one another with these words.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote to the Christians in Thessalonica.
He told them about the return of the Lord Jesus Christ.
He said the Lord will come down from heaven.
He said the dead in Christ will rise first.
He said those who are alive will join them in the clouds.
He said all believers will meet the Lord in the air.
He said believers will always be with the Lord.
Therefore, encourage one another with these words.
passages.original: Ὥστε παρακαλεῖτε ἀλλήλους ἐν τοῖς λόγοις τούτοις
